title: Global secondary indexes and the query that degenerates into a scan

videos.script: Lesson 9 left one question without a key. Every order of one day, across all customers. {{question}} The table cannot name a partition for it, so it reads everything. {{scan}} You will watch that scan go through the table one megabyte at a time. A filter makes the answer smaller. It does not make the reading smaller, and the bill follows the reading. {{pages}} Then you will build a second copy of the orders, keyed by the day. That is a global secondary index. {{index}} The same question becomes one page, for about a fortieth of the cost. {{query}} An index can also hold only the items in one state, such as the orders still waiting for delivery. {{sparse}} And you will meet the local index, the one that can only be created with the table. {{local}}
